In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] discipline of [[algebraic geometry]], '''Serre's theorem on affineness''' (also called '''Serre's cohomological characterization of affineness''' or '''Serre's criterion on affineness''') is a theorem due to [[Jean-Pierre Serre]] which gives sufficient conditions for a [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]] to be [[Spectrum of a ring|affine]], stated in terms of [[sheaf cohomology]].<ref>{{harvtxt|Stacks 01XF}}.</ref> The theorem was first published by Serre in 1957.<ref>{{harvtxt|Serre |1957}}.</ref>

==Statement==
Let {{math|''X''}} be a scheme with [[Sheaf (mathematics)#Ringed spaces and locally ringed spaces|structure sheaf]] {{math|''O''<sub>''X''</sub>.}} If:
:(1) {{math|''X''}} is quasi-compact, and
:(2) for every [[quasi-coherent]] [[ideal sheaf]] {{math|''I''}} of {{math|''O''<sub>''X''</sub>}}-modules, {{math|''H''<sup>1</sup>(''X'', ''I'') {{=}} 0}},{{efn|Some texts, such as {{harvtxt |Ueno |2001 |pp=128–133 }}, require that {{math|''H''<sup>''i''</sup>(''X'',''I'')&nbsp;{{=}}&nbsp;''0''}} for all {{math|''i''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;1}} as a condition for the theorem. In fact, this is equivalent to condition (2) above.}}
then {{math|''X''}} is [[Spectrum of a ring|affine]].<ref>{{harvtxt|Stacks 01XF}}.</ref>

==Related results==
* A special case of this theorem arises when {{mvar|''X''}} is an [[algebraic variety]], in which case the conditions of the theorem imply that {{mvar|''X''}} is an [[affine variety]].
* A similar result has stricter conditions on {{mvar|''X''}} but looser conditions on the cohomology: if {{mvar|''X''}} is a [[quasi-separated]], quasi-compact scheme, and if {{math|''H''<sup>1</sup>(''X'',&nbsp;''I'')&nbsp;{{=}}&nbsp;0}} for any quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals {{mvar|''I''}} of finite type, then {{mvar|''X''}} is affine.<ref>{{harvtxt|Stacks 01XE}}, Lemma 29.3.2.</ref>
